title: Idle world: the sea-stack that fell over with nobody playing
question: In the fixed run, does the ground now read as at rest — or is there still something coming apart that shouldn't be?
context_md:
Your report: ground breaking after just waiting at startup. It reproduces with **no verb of any kind applied** — this is `worldcrack` with the strike turned off, so nothing in either run is the player.

Same seed, same frames, same times of day (frames 902 / 2102 / 3302). The only difference is the fix.

Cause: when the ground root was given a real distance last week, one function that reads it (`dependants`) was left behind, so two boulders sitting on the same scree slope started being treated as though the lower one were carrying the upper — all the way down the hill, until the rock at the foot was reckoned to be holding up the entire hillside and gave way.

**What I am unsure about and would like your eye on:** whether the fixed run still loses anything it shouldn't. It is not zero — 76 cells of rock still go, against 1,756 — and I do not know whether what remains is honest weathering or the tail of the same bug.

items.label: before — on main
